Across these problems, successful approaches combine task-specific objectives with transferable features, structured priors, and differentiable optimization. The review concludes by identifying open directions in generalization, efficient learning, trustworthy evaluation, and the integration of visual perception with downstream decision-making systems.

original_abstract: In this work we introduce a new self-supervised, semi-parametric approach for synthesizing novel views of a vehicle starting from a single monocular image. Differently from parametric (i.e. entirely learning-based) methods, we show how a-priori geometric knowledge about the object and the 3D world can be successfully integrated into a deep learning based image generation framework. As this geometric component is not learnt, we call our approach semi-parametric. #R##N#In particular, we exploit man-made object symmetry and piece-wise planarity to integrate rich a-priori visual information into the novel viewpoint synthesis process. An Image Completion Network (ICN) is then trained to generate a realistic image starting from this geometric guidance. #R##N#This careful blend between parametric and non-parametric components allows us to i) operate in a real-world scenario, ii) preserve high-frequency visual information such as textures, iii) handle truly arbitrary 3D roto-translations of the input and iv) perform shape transfer to completely different 3D models. Eventually, we show that our approach can be easily complemented with synthetic data and extended to other rigid objects with completely different topology, even in presence of concave structures and holes (e.g. chairs). #R##N#A comprehensive experimental analysis against state-of-the-art competitors shows the efficacy of our method both from a quantitative and a perceptive point of view. #R##N#Supplementary material, animated results, code and data are available at: this https URL

Through comparisons across representative datasets and tasks, we identify common strengths and limitations of current methods. original_abstract: Deep learning based methods have achieved surprising progress in Scene Text Recognition (STR), one of classic problems in computer vision. In this paper, we propose a feasible framework for multi-lingual arbitrary-shaped STR, including instance segmentation based text detection and language model based attention mechanism for text recognition. Our STR algorithm not only recognizes Latin and Non-Latin characters, but also supports arbitrary-shaped text recognition. Our method wins the championship on Scene Text Spotting Task (Latin Only, Latin and Chinese) of ICDAR2019 Robust Reading Challenge on ArbitraryShaped Text Competition. Code is available at this https URL.

original_abstract: We are witnessing a confluence of vision, speech and dialog system technologies that are enabling the IVAs to learn audio-visual groundings of utterances and have conversations with users about the objects, activities and events surrounding them. Recent progress in visual grounding techniques and Audio Understanding are enabling machines to understand shared semantic concepts and listen to the various sensory events in the environment. With audio and visual grounding methods, end-to-end multimodal SDS are trained to meaningfully communicate with us in natural language about the real dynamic audio-visual sensory world around us. In this work, we explore the role of `topics' as the context of the conversation along with multimodal attention into such an end-to-end audio-visual scene-aware dialog system architecture. We also incorporate an end-to-end audio classification ConvNet, AclNet, into our models. We develop and test our approaches on the Audio Visual Scene-Aware Dialog (AVSD) dataset released as a part of the DSTC7. We present the analysis of our experiments and show that some of our model variations outperform the baseline system released for AVSD.

We also examine approaches for discovering previously unseen intents, estimating word-usage similarity, recognizing scientific entities, and detecting phishing through syntactic evidence. For structured language understanding and generation, we discuss transition-based AMR parsing, graph-aware AMR-to-text generation, and intermediate representations for complex cross-domain Text-to-SQL. Finally, we analyze extractive and abstractive summarization methods that incorporate latent sentence selection, entailment, question generation, and layer-specific parameter sharing, together with transformers for unaligned multimodal sequences. Across these areas, the reviewed work demonstrates the value of explicit structure, weak or indirect supervision, adaptive attention, and shared representations. We identify persistent challenges involving data sparsity, domain transfer, interpretability, computational cost, and reliable evaluation, and outline directions toward robust, flexible, and genuinely universal language technologies.

original_abstract: Recent efforts show that neural networks are vulnerable to small but intentional perturbations on input features in visual classification tasks. Due to the additional consideration of connections between examples (\eg articles with citation link tend to be in the same class), graph neural networks could be more sensitive to the perturbations, since the perturbations from connected examples exacerbate the impact on a target example. Adversarial Training (AT), a dynamic regularization technique, can resist the worst-case perturbations on input features and is a promising choice to improve model robustness and generalization. However, existing AT methods focus on standard classification, being less effective when training models on graph since it does not model the impact from connected examples.  In this work, we explore adversarial training on graph, aiming to improve the robustness and generalization of models learned on graph. We propose Graph Adversarial Training (GraphAT), which takes the impact from connected examples into account when learning to construct and resist perturbations. We give a general formulation of GraphAT, which can be seen as a dynamic regularization scheme based on the graph structure. To demonstrate the utility of GraphAT, we employ it on a state-of-the-art graph neural network model --- Graph Convolutional Network (GCN). We conduct experiments on two citation graphs (Citeseer and Cora) and a knowledge graph (NELL), verifying the effectiveness of GraphAT which outperforms normal training on GCN by 4.51% in node classification accuracy. Codes are available via: https://github.com/fulifeng/GraphAT.

We discuss how architectural depth, learned representations, attention, graph structure, and hierarchical modeling support generalization, optimization, and transfer across tasks. We also examine methods for uncertainty quantification, interpretability, robustness to adversarial and distributional changes, fairness, privacy, and efficient training and deployment. Particular attention is given to generative adversarial and variational models, neural approaches to structured prediction, few-shot and domain adaptation, and learning under limited feedback or computation. Alongside empirical successes, we summarize theoretical perspectives on loss landscapes, convergence, sample complexity, information leakage, and approximation. The review highlights persistent limitations, including reliance on large and potentially biased datasets, poor calibration, vulnerability to shifts and attacks, and limited causal and semantic understanding. We conclude by identifying research directions toward models that are more data-efficient, transparent, reliable, resource-conscious, and aligned with human objectives.

original_abstract: Executable semantic parsing is the task of converting natural language utterances into logical forms that can be directly used as queries to get a response. We build a transfer learning framework for executable semantic parsing. We show that the framework is effective for Question Answering (QA we experiment with public data sets such as Overnight and NLmaps as well as with commercial SLU data. The experiments carried out on data sets that are different in nature show how executable semantic parsing can unify different areas of NLP such as Q&A and SLU.

We examine contextual and subword embeddings, recurrent, convolutional, attention-based, and Transformer architectures, as well as models for syntax, semantics, morphology, discourse, dialogue, translation, information extraction, classification, and generation. Particular attention is given to learning with limited or noisy supervision, including semi-supervised, distant, unsupervised, cross-lingual, and counterfactual settings. We also discuss approaches that incorporate external knowledge, multimodal evidence, document context, and human feedback. Across these areas, we identify recurring challenges involving compositionality, long-range dependencies, robustness to domain shift, interpretability, efficiency, and evaluation. The review highlights how architectural constraints and carefully designed representations can improve systematic and zero-shot generalization, while also exposing limitations of current benchmarks and metrics. We conclude with open research directions toward more data-efficient, multilingual, knowledge-aware, and human-aligned language technologies.

original_abstract: The redundancy is widely recognized in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which enables to remove unimportant filters from convolutional layers so as to slim the network with acceptable performance drop. Inspired by the linear and combinational properties of convolution, we seek to make some filters increasingly close and eventually identical for network slimming. To this end, we propose Centripetal SGD (C-SGD), a novel optimization method, which can train several filters to collapse into a single point in the parameter hyperspace. When the training is completed, the removal of the identical filters can trim the network with NO performance loss, thus no finetuning is needed. By doing so, we have partly solved an open problem of constrained filter pruning on CNNs with complicated structure, where some layers must be pruned following others. Our experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet have justified the effectiveness of C-SGD-based filter pruning. Moreover, we have provided empirical evidences for the assumption that the redundancy in deep neural networks helps the convergence of training by showing that a redundant CNN trained using C-SGD outperforms a normally trained counterpart with the equivalent width.

We discuss advances in model compression, sparse and resource-efficient computation, automated hyperparameter and algorithm selection, variance reduction, approximate inference, and differentiable integration of combinatorial solvers. Across these areas, we identify recurring trade-offs between predictive accuracy, computational cost, data requirements, transparency, and reliability. By bringing together theoretical analyses, algorithmic innovations, and application-driven studies, this work highlights common principles underlying current progress and outlines open challenges for developing machine learning systems that are efficient, trustworthy, and effective in real-world settings.

original_abstract: Implicit discourse relation recognition is a challenging task due to the absence of the necessary informative clue from explicit connectives. The prediction of relations requires a deep understanding of the semantic meanings of sentence pairs. As implicit discourse relation recognizer has to carefully tackle the semantic similarity of the given sentence pairs and the severe data sparsity issue exists in the meantime, it is supposed to be beneficial from mastering the entire training data. Thus in this paper, we propose a novel memory mechanism to tackle the challenges for further performance improvement. The memory mechanism is adequately memorizing information by pairing representations and discourse relations of all training instances, which right fills the slot of the data-hungry issue in the current implicit discourse relation recognizer. Our experiments show that our full model with memorizing the entire training set reaches new state-of-the-art against strong baselines, which especially for the first time exceeds the milestone of 60% accuracy in the 4-way task.

The review concludes by outlining open challenges, including reliable evaluation, learning from limited and heterogeneous data, modeling context and pragmatics, mitigating bias, and developing systems whose internal reasoning and outputs can be understood and trusted by users.

original_abstract: Modern object detectors can rarely achieve short training time, fast inference speed, and high accuracy at the same time. To strike a balance among them, we propose the Training-Time-Friendly Network (TTFNet). In this work, we start with light-head, single-stage, and anchor-free designs, which enable fast inference speed. Then, we focus on shortening training time. We notice that encoding more training samples from annotated boxes plays a similar role as increasing batch size, which helps enlarge the learning rate and accelerate the training process. To this end, we introduce a novel approach using Gaussian kernels to encode training samples. Besides, we design the initiative sample weights for better information utilization. Experiments on MS COCO show that our TTFNet has great advantages in balancing training time, inference speed, and accuracy. It has reduced training time by more than seven times compared to previous real-time detectors while maintaining state-of-the-art performances. In addition, our super-fast version of TTFNet-18 and TTFNet-53 can outperform SSD300 and YOLOv3 by less than one-tenth of their training time, respectively. The code has been made available at \url{https://github.com/ZJULearning/ttfnet}.

We organize existing methods according to their principal mechanisms: architectural design, representation learning, structured prediction, generative modeling, sequential inference, and optimization. Particular attention is given to convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, adversarial, reversible, and low-precision networks, as well as techniques for exploiting synthetic data, auxiliary tasks, class relationships, and unlabeled examples. We discuss applications ranging from semantic segmentation and object detection to scene text retrieval, human and animal tracking, medical image analysis, face recognition, depth estimation, physical reasoning, and video question answering. Across these domains, successful systems combine task-specific inductive biases with end-to-end learning while addressing efficiency, robustness, interpretability, and data scarcity. We conclude by identifying open challenges in scalable training, reliable evaluation, privacy-preserving visual analysis, and the development of models that generalize across sensors, environments, tasks, and levels of visual abstraction.

original_abstract: Storage resources and caching techniques permeate almost every area of communication networks today. In the near future, caching is set to play an important role in storage-assisted Internet architectures, information-centric networks, and wireless systems, reducing operating and capital expenditures and improving the services offered to users. In light of the remarkable data traffic growth and the increasing number of rich-media applications, the impact of caching is expected to become even more profound than it is today. Therefore, it is crucial to design these systems in an optimal fashion, ensuring the maximum possible performance and economic benefits from their deployment. To this end, this article presents a collection of detailed models and algorithms, which are synthesized to build a powerful analytical framework for caching optimization.

We examine developments in 5G and beyond, including network slicing, heterogeneous and millimeter-wave networks, device-to-device communication, full-duplex transmission, software-defined and information-centric networking, edge and fog computing, and opportunistic infrastructure. We further discuss traffic engineering, caching, service migration, task offloading, routing, scheduling, power control, and topology design, emphasizing approaches based on optimization, game theory, stochastic modeling, machine learning, and reinforcement learning. original_abstract: Neuromorphic computing takes inspiration from the brain to create energy efficient hardware for information processing, capable of highly sophisticated tasks. In this article, we make the case that building this new hardware necessitates reinventing electronics. We show that research in physics and material science will be key to create artificial nano-neurons and synapses, to connect them together in huge numbers, to organize them in complex systems, and to compute with them efficiently. We describe how some researchers choose to take inspiration from artificial intelligence to move forward in this direction, whereas others prefer taking inspiration from neuroscience, and we highlight recent striking results obtained with these two approaches. Finally, we discuss the challenges and perspectives in neuromorphic physics, which include developing the algorithms and the hardware hand in hand, making significant advances with small toy systems, as well as building large scale networks.
generated_abstract: Unconventional computing explores computational models that exploit physical dynamics, material properties, and biological organization beyond the conventional von Neumann architecture. This paper surveys emerging approaches spanning memristive and spintronic circuits, stochastic and spiking neural hardware, photonic and chemical reaction networks, molecular communication, quantum and oscillator-based optimization, and programmable biological matter. We examine how memory, nonlinearity, stochasticity, self-organization, and massive parallelism can be used to perform inference, learning, logic, optimization, and communication at low energy and high density. Particular attention is given to the relationship between device physics and computational abstraction, including the challenges of mapping algorithms onto imperfect substrates, handling variability and noise, and evaluating performance at the application level. We compare these platforms in terms of scalability, programmability, accuracy, latency, energy efficiency, and technological maturity. The review also considers hybrid architectures that combine unconventional devices with CMOS and conventional processors, thereby balancing physical efficiency with numerical precision and software flexibility. Finally, we identify open problems in benchmarking, verification, fabrication, system integration, and the definition of computation itself, and outline directions toward robust, application-driven unconventional computing systems.

original_abstract: Contextual representation models have achieved great success in improving various downstream tasks. However, these language-model-based encoders are difficult to train due to the large parameter sizes and high computational complexity. By carefully examining the training procedure, we find that the softmax layer (the output layer) causes significant inefficiency due to the large vocabulary size. Therefore, we redesign the learning objective and propose an efficient framework for training contextual representation models. Specifically, the proposed approach bypasses the softmax layer by performing language modeling with dimension reduction, and allows the models to leverage pre-trained word embeddings. Our framework reduces the time spent on the output layer to a negligible level, eliminates almost all the trainable parameters of the softmax layer and performs language modeling without truncating the vocabulary. When applied to ELMo, our method achieves a 4 times speedup and eliminates 80% trainable parameters while achieving competitive performance on downstream tasks.

We further consider their application to tagging, information extraction, sentiment analysis, question answering, machine translation, dialogue, summarization, speech recognition, and text generation. Particular attention is given to low-resource settings, where limited annotation, imperfect lexicons, and domain variation require weak supervision, active learning, unsupervised training, or adaptation from related languages. Through comparison of established benchmarks and representative systems, we analyze the contributions of structure-aware encoders, pretrained language models, multimodal signals, reinforcement learning, and interpretable representations. The results highlight consistent gains from incorporating linguistic or relational structure, while also revealing limitations in compositional generalization, fairness, transparency, and evaluation. We conclude by identifying practical directions for scalable, multilingual, and more reliable NLP systems.

original_abstract: There is a growing interest in learning a model which could recognize novel classes with only a few labeled examples. In this paper, we propose Temporal Alignment Module (TAM), a novel few-shot learning framework that can learn to classify a previous unseen video. While most previous works neglect long-term temporal ordering information, our proposed model explicitly leverages the temporal ordering information in video data through temporal alignment. This leads to strong data-efficiency for few-shot learning. In concrete, TAM calculates the distance value of query video with respect to novel class proxies by averaging the per frame distances along its alignment path. We introduce continuous relaxation to TAM so the model can be learned in an end-to-end fashion to directly optimize the few-shot learning objective. We evaluate TAM on two challenging real-world datasets, Kinetics and Something-Something-V2, and show that our model leads to significant improvement of few-shot video classification over a wide range of competitive baselines.
generated_abstract: Deep learning has transformed computer vision, enabling substantial progress in image understanding, generation, restoration, tracking, three-dimensional analysis, and multimodal perception. This paper presents a structured review of recent methods and applications across these areas. We examine convolutional and competitive pathway architectures, normalization and attention mechanisms, representation learning, and model compression for efficient recognition. We further discuss generative approaches for stylization, attribute editing, pose-guided synthesis, domain adaptation, and removal of rain, haze, and blur. For structured visual data, we review techniques for crowd counting, point-cloud classification and recognition, photometric stereo, aerial scanning, and video instance segmentation. Applications involving human behavior and identity, including sentiment recognition, action-unit detection, re-identification, tracking, and navigation, are also considered. Medical and scientific imaging illustrate the benefits and remaining challenges of learning from limited or costly annotations. Particular attention is given to weak supervision, synthetic data, transfer learning, interpretability, and computational efficiency. By comparing objectives, data requirements, evaluation protocols, and practical limitations, the paper identifies common design principles and open problems, and outlines promising directions toward robust, explainable, and deployable computer vision systems.

original_abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown huge superiority over humans in image recognition, speech processing, autonomous vehicles and medical diagnosis. However, recent studies indicate that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial examples (AEs), which are designed by attackers to fool deep learning models. Different from real examples, AEs can mislead the model to predict incorrect outputs while hardly be distinguished by human eyes, therefore threaten security-critical deep-learning applications. In recent years, the generation and defense of AEs have become a research hotspot in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) security. This article reviews the latest research progress of AEs. First, we introduce the concept, cause, characteristics and evaluation metrics of AEs, then give a survey on the state-of-the-art AE generation methods with the discussion of advantages and disadvantages. After that, we review the existing defenses and discuss their limitations. Finally, future research opportunities and challenges on AEs are prospected.
generated_abstract: This paper presents a unified perspective on contemporary machine learning methods for learning from limited, distributed, noisy, and structured data. We organize recent advances around four recurring challenges: reducing the effective complexity of models, transferring knowledge across tasks and domains, making decisions under uncertainty, and incorporating structure or prior knowledge into learning. The discussion covers intrinsic dimensionality, random and semi-random features, tensor and matrix factorization, graph-based and temporal representations, and constrained or interpretable neural architectures. We further examine active and semi-supervised learning, federated and privacy-preserving optimization, robust classification, uncertainty calibration, and safe exploration in reinforcement learning. Particular attention is given to the interaction between statistical guarantees and practical scalability, including online, asynchronous, and distributed algorithms. Across applications in healthcare, brain decoding, intelligent transportation, energy systems, cybersecurity, and autonomous control, we highlight common design principles: exploit reusable structure, quantify confidence, adapt to changing environments, and align models with domain constraints. The resulting synthesis identifies open problems in reliable representation learning, efficient inference, and principled transfer, and suggests directions for developing machine learning systems that are both high-performing and trustworthy.

original_abstract: We develop new abstractions for reasoning about three relaxations of differential privacy:  $R$ enyi differential privacy, zero-concentrated differential privacy, and truncated concentrated differential privacy, which express bounds on statistical divergences between two output probability distributions. In order to reason about such properties compositionally, we introduce approximate span-lifting, a novel construction extending the approximate relational lifting approaches previously developed for standard differential privacy to a more general class of divergences, and also to continuous distributions. As an application, we develop a program logic based on approximate span-liftings capable of proving relaxations of differential privacy and other statistical divergence properties.
generated_abstract: Modern software increasingly combines concurrency, rich type systems, numerical computation, and low-level data manipulation, making reliable reasoning about programs difficult. This paper presents a unified framework for the analysis and transformation of such programs. The framework combines executable operational semantics with type- and specification-guided static analysis, enabling programmers to describe data formats, communication protocols, ownership constraints, and numerical invariants within a common semantic setting. It supports both safety-oriented verification, including memory safety, deadlock freedom, communication correctness, termination, and floating-point test stability, and semantics-preserving program transformations such as automatic differentiation and tensor-aware computation. To control the cost of analysis, the framework incorporates symbolic execution, partial-order reduction, and targeted generation of initial concurrent configurations. We establish soundness results for the principal analyses and identify conditions under which inference is complete or decidable, while also characterizing inherent undecidability in expressive dependent type systems. Mechanized semantic models and prototype implementations demonstrate that the approach scales to representative functional, imperative, concurrent, and scientific programs. The results suggest that combining precise language semantics with domain-specific specifications can provide practical verification without sacrificing abstraction or programming flexibility.

original_abstract: Although deep neural networks have been successful in image classification, they are prone to adversarial attacks. To generate misclassified inputs, there has emerged a wide variety of techniques, such as black- and whitebox testing of neural networks. In this paper, we present DeepSearch, a novel blackbox-fuzzing technique for image classifiers. Despite its simplicity, DeepSearch is shown to be more effective in finding adversarial examples than closely related black- and whitebox approaches. DeepSearch is additionally able to generate the most subtle adversarial examples in comparison to these approaches.
generated_abstract: Machine learning has advanced rapidly across healthcare, sensing, recommendation, robotics, scientific computing, and decision support, yet reliable deployment remains limited by challenges in data, computation, generalization, interpretability, privacy, fairness, and robustness. This paper presents a broad framework for developing practical learning systems that address these challenges jointly. We review methods for learning from heterogeneous, incomplete, distributed, and weakly labeled data, including federated, semi-supervised, multitask, graph-based, and generative approaches. We examine representations and architectures for temporal, spatial, relational, and continuous dynamical data, together with techniques for causal discovery and reinforcement learning. To support deployment, we discuss scalable optimization, adaptive computation, model compression, quantization, low-rank approximation, efficient convolution, and hardware-aware inference. We further analyze uncertainty estimation, adversarial robustness, fairness, individual-level guarantees, and information-theoretic explanations. Across representative applications, we emphasize the importance of evaluating not only predictive accuracy but also sample efficiency, computational cost, privacy, stability, and transparency. The resulting perspective identifies common principles underlying modern learning systems and highlights open problems in building models that are accurate, efficient, adaptable, trustworthy, and suitable for resource-constrained real-world environments.

original_abstract: We simulate data using a graphic engine to augment real-world datasets, with application to vehicle re-identification (re-ID). In order for data augmentation to be effective, the simulated data should be similar to the real data in key attributes like illumination and viewpoint. We introduce a large-scale synthetic dataset VehicleX. Created in Unity, it contains 1,209 vehicles of various models in 3D with fully editable attributes. We propose an attribute descent approach to let VehicleX approximate the attributes in real-world datasets. Specifically, we manipulate each attribute in VehicleX, aiming to minimize the discrepancy between VehicleX and real data in terms of the Fr'echet Inception Distance (FID). This attribute descent algorithm allows content-level domain adaptation (DA), which has advantages over existing DA methods working on the pixel level or feature level. We mix adapted VehicleX data with three vehicle re-ID datasets individually, and observe consistent improvement when the proposed attribute descent is applied. With the augmented datasets, we report competitive accuracy compared with state-of-the-art results. The VehicleX engine and code of this paper will be released.
generated_abstract: Deep learning has transformed computer vision by enabling robust representations for recognition, localization, tracking, segmentation, reconstruction, and multimodal understanding. However, progress has produced a diverse and rapidly expanding body of methods whose relationships, assumptions, and practical trade-offs are difficult to assess. This paper presents a unified review of recent advances in visual learning, organizing them according to the mechanisms used to improve representation, generalization, efficiency, and interpretability. We discuss attention and relational reasoning, temporal and geometric modeling, weak and zero-shot supervision, domain adaptation, synthetic data generation, uncertainty estimation, and constrained or continual learning. We further examine specialized architectures for multi-task learning, video analysis, stereo and depth estimation, medical imaging, remote sensing, and human-centered applications. Across these settings, we highlight recurring challenges, including limited and biased annotations, distribution shift, occlusion, computational cost, catastrophic forgetting, and the need for reliable confidence estimates. By connecting methodological developments with representative applications, the review identifies common design principles and open research directions toward visual systems that are more data-efficient, adaptive, interpretable, and dependable in real-world environments.

original_abstract: Designing a molecule with desired properties is one of the biggest challenges in drug development, as it requires optimization of chemical compound structures with respect to many complex properties. To augment the compound design process we introduce Mol-CycleGAN - a CycleGAN-based model that generates optimized compounds with high structural similarity to the original ones. Namely, given a molecule our model generates a structurally similar one with an optimized value of the considered property. We evaluate the performance of the model on selected optimization objectives related to structural properties (presence of halogen groups, number of aromatic rings) and to a physicochemical property (penalized logP). In the task of optimization of penalized logP of drug-like molecules our model significantly outperforms previous results.
generated_abstract: Machine learning is advancing rapidly across supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement-learning settings, but progress depends increasingly on addressing limitations beyond predictive accuracy. This paper reviews recent methods that improve the efficiency, scalability, adaptability, and reliability of learning systems. We consider biologically motivated alternatives to backpropagation, variance-reduced and second-order optimization, compact parameterizations for high-dimensional inputs, and knowledge distillation for deploying generative models on resource-constrained hardware. We also examine data-centric strategies, including efficient augmentation, standardized multi-label data management, active acquisition of side information, and zero-shot prediction through semantic representations. For sequential decision-making, we discuss curriculum design, retrospective imitation, adaptive traffic control, exploration in ranking systems, and physically informed objectives for robust, symmetric, and energy-efficient behavior. Finally, we address structural and societal challenges, including clustering and low-rank approximation, privacy risks caused by overlearning sensitive attributes, and the difficulty of controlling unintended representations. Taken together, these studies illustrate a shift from building larger models toward designing learning systems that use data and computation judiciously, transfer knowledge effectively, provide stronger guarantees, and remain safe and useful in real-world applications.

original_abstract: Reconstructing 3D human shape and pose from a monocular image is challenging despite the promising results achieved by the most recent learning-based methods. The commonly occurred misalignment comes from the facts that the mapping from images to the model space is highly non-linear and the rotation-based pose representation of the body model is prone to result in the drift of joint positions. In this work, we investigate learning 3D human shape and pose from dense correspondences of body parts and propose a Decompose-and-aggregate Network (DaNet) to address these issues. DaNet adopts the dense correspondence maps, which densely build a bridge between 2D pixels and 3D vertexes, as intermediate representations to facilitate the learning of 2D-to-3D mapping. The prediction modules of DaNet are decomposed into one global stream and multiple local streams to enable global and fine-grained perceptions for the shape and pose predictions, respectively. Messages from local streams are further aggregated to enhance the robust prediction of the rotation-based poses, where a position-aided rotation feature refinement strategy is proposed to exploit spatial relationships between body joints. Moreover, a Part-based Dropout (PartDrop) strategy is introduced to drop out dense information from intermediate representations during training, encouraging the network to focus on more complementary body parts as well as adjacent position features. The effectiveness of our method is validated on both in-door and real-world datasets including the Human3.6M, UP3D, and DensePose-COCO datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves the reconstruction performance in comparison with previous state-of-the-art methods. Our code will be made publicly available at this https URL .
generated_abstract: Deep learning has transformed computer vision by enabling models to learn increasingly expressive representations directly from images, videos, depth measurements, and multimodal sensor data. This paper presents a broad review of recent learning-based methods for visual analysis, emphasizing how architectural design, prior knowledge, and supervision influence performance. We organize the literature into major tasks, including image restoration and enhancement, segmentation, object detection and recognition, retrieval, pose and shape estimation, tracking, activity understanding, image and video generation, and medical and scientific imaging. We examine convolutional, recurrent, adversarial, graph-based, attention, and generative models, together with approaches for few-shot, zero-shot, weakly supervised, unsupervised, and domain-adaptive learning. Particular attention is given to methods that address limited annotation, noisy labels, domain shift, computational constraints, and the need for physically or semantically meaningful representations. We compare representative datasets and evaluation practices and discuss the complementary roles of data-driven learning and model-based priors. Finally, we identify open challenges in robustness, interpretability, scalability, efficiency, and deployment, outlining promising directions for reliable vision systems in real-world environments.

original_abstract: Land cover classification of remote sensing images is a challenging task due to limited amounts of annotated data, highly imbalanced classes, frequent incorrect pixel-level annotations, and an inherent complexity in the semantic segmentation task. In this article, we propose a novel architecture called the dense dilated convolutions' merging network (DDCM-Net) to address this task. The proposed DDCM-Net consists of dense dilated image convolutions merged with varying dilation rates. This effectively utilizes rich combinations of dilated convolutions that enlarge the network's receptive fields with fewer parameters and features compared with the state-of-the-art approaches in the remote sensing domain. Importantly, DDCM-Net obtains fused local- and global-context information, in effect incorporating surrounding discriminative capability for multiscale and complex-shaped objects with similar color and textures in very high-resolution aerial imagery. We demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and flexibility of the proposed DDCM-Net on the publicly available ISPRS Potsdam and Vaihingen data sets, as well as the DeepGlobe land cover data set. Our single model, trained on three-band Potsdam and Vaihingen data sets, achieves better accuracy in terms of both mean intersection over union (mIoU) and F1-score compared with other published models trained with more than three-band data. We further validate our model on the DeepGlobe data set, achieving state-of-the-art result 56.2% mIoU with much fewer parameters and at a lower computational cost compared with related recent work. Code available at https://github.com/samleoqh/DDCM-Semantic-Segmentation-PyTorch
generated_abstract: Deep learning has transformed computer vision by enabling unified, data-driven solutions for recognition, reconstruction, segmentation, detection, and multimodal understanding. This paper reviews recent advances in deep neural architectures and examines how representation learning, attention mechanisms, recurrent models, generative modeling, self-supervision, meta-learning, and differentiable optimization are applied across diverse visual tasks. We organize existing methods according to their objectives, data requirements, and underlying architectural principles, covering face and biometric analysis, object detection and recognition, semantic and instance segmentation, image restoration, medical image analysis, gesture and video understanding, and language-guided vision. Particular attention is given to robustness under blur, noise, low resolution, domain shift, limited supervision, and changing viewpoints. We also discuss emerging concerns involving privacy, demographic bias, dataset imbalance, and the reliability of evaluation metrics. By comparing representative approaches and their reported performance on standard benchmarks, the paper identifies common strengths and limitations of current systems. Finally, we outline promising directions for efficient, interpretable, fair, and privacy-preserving vision models capable of learning from heterogeneous data and operating reliably in real-world environments.

original_abstract: We propose a novel text generation task, namely Curiosity-driven Question Generation. We start from the observation that the Question Generation task has traditionally been considered as the dual problem of Question Answering, hence tackling the problem of generating a question given the text that contains its answer. Such questions can be used to evaluate machine reading comprehension. However, in real life, and especially in conversational settings, humans tend to ask questions with the goal of enriching their knowledge and/or clarifying aspects of previously gathered information. We refer to these inquisitive questions as Curiosity-driven: these questions are generated with the goal of obtaining new information (the answer) which is not present in the input text. In this work, we experiment on this new task using a conversational Question Answering (QA) dataset; further, since the majority of QA dataset are not built in a conversational manner, we describe a methodology to derive data for this novel task from non-conversational QA data. We investigate several automated metrics to measure the different properties of Curious Questions, and experiment different approaches on the Curiosity-driven Question Generation task, including model pre-training and reinforcement learning. Finally, we report a qualitative evaluation of the generated outputs.
generated_abstract: Natural language processing has advanced rapidly through neural representation learning, attention mechanisms, pretrained language models, and increasingly diverse sources of supervision. This paper provides a broad overview of contemporary methods for analyzing and generating human language, covering machine translation, sentiment and irony detection, information extraction, semantic parsing, relation and event extraction, dialogue systems, question answering, summarization, document understanding, and text generation. We organize existing approaches according to their use of linguistic structure, external knowledge, multimodal information, weak or distant supervision, and retrieval. Particular attention is given to methods that address limited labeled data, domain shift, rare and unknown words, computational cost, interpretability, and fairness. We also review emerging resources and evaluation settings, including conversational, biomedical, legal, social-media, and multilingual data. Across tasks, neural architectures generally improve predictive performance, but their effectiveness depends on data quality, suitable representations, and careful evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy. The review concludes by identifying open challenges in robust generalization, efficient inference, responsible deployment, knowledge integration, and the reliable assessment of generated language, emphasizing the need for systems that combine statistical learning with explicit structure and human-centered evaluation.
